question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class operator internal `session:end` event, or route this workflow-integration use case to the existing typed plugin `session_end` hook?
rationale: Current main has a robust plugin lifecycle hook but no internal hook event; choosing between these surfaces changes the public extension contract and should not be decided by cleanup automation.

options.title: Document plugin surface
options.body: Treat typed plugin `session_end` as the supported lifecycle integration surface and update internal-hook docs to point workflow users there.

options.title: Add internal event
options.body: Add `session:end` to the internal `HOOK.md` surface and wire it consistently across reset, compaction, delete, shutdown, subagent, cron, and agent-completion paths.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until the broader session/subagent lifecycle contract is settled with related issues and PRs.

recommendation.title: Document plugin surface
recommendation.body: Treat typed plugin `session_end` as the supported lifecycle integration surface and update internal-hook docs to point workflow users there.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision hinges on plugin hook versus internal hook contract boundaries, and recent history shows Vincent working on adjacent plugin hook surfaces.
